title: Ten Reasons It's Good
author: Dave Stuart Jr.
summary: Stuart shares a self-care exercise he calls "Ten Reasons It's Good," designed to relieve the spiritual pain that comes from doing demanding work without feeling motivated to do it. The practice is simple: list ten reasons, kept broad and unedited, why the work you do is good, and he models the exercise live with ten small, specific moments from his own teaching life — a colleague's mustache, a struggling student's progress, a shared joke with a class. He's candid that the list took effort to complete and that his mind kept drifting toward reasons it's not good, which he frames as a normal part of the process rather than a failure of it. He's careful to note the exercise isn't a comprehensive accounting of the job's hard realities and isn't a silver bullet, but rather a modest, repeatable way to relieve pressure inside a teacher's soul.
points: Stuart frames teacher demotivation as producing genuine "spiritual pain," giving the exercise emotional stakes beyond generic self-care advice.
The exercise's power lies in its constraint — ten items, unedited, kept broad — which forces specificity rather than vague gratitude statements.
By modeling the exercise transparently, including his own mental drift toward negatives, Stuart normalizes the difficulty of the practice rather than presenting it as effortless positivity.
He's explicit that the exercise is meant to stay private in normal use, since "the value of it is the doing of it," not the sharing of it.
quotes: When a human soul is demotivated to do a task that soul is nonetheless required to do, the result is spiritual pain.

Thankfully, there are things we can do for our souls to make demotivation less a specter in our daily experience. They aren't magical silver bullets that make us forever motivated, but they are exercises that reliably help.
All that you do is, on a blank document or sheet of paper, create a list of ten reasons why the work that you do is good. Keep that word "good" in mind — let it be elemental and broad.
It took me some time to get to ten. In the process, my mind meandered — sometimes to the reasons it's not good.

I had to repeatedly remind myself that the goal here wasn't to give myself a perfectly accurate picture of what my practice is like. It's to list ten reasons why my practice is good, ten ways in which I've experienced it as good lately.
In short, while these lists are NOT comprehensive and do NOT do anything about the hard realities of our jobs, what they do accomplish is relieving a bit of pressure inside our souls.
